answer: A depreciating identity bond makes idle identities lose value. Each identity posts a 100-credit bond decaying 10 per idle epoch, like an opal fading unless its owner keeps working. At a glacier pace that never pauses, a parked fake is worthless after ten epochs. Renewal needs work bound to that bond, so the k-th fake still needs its own 100 credits and work record; 1,000 fakes cost 100,000 credits, no bulk discount. Bond laundering, reusing one receipt for many bonds, fails: each receipt bears a copper seal usable only once. An honest agent posts one bond and keeps value by working once.
